sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The unprecedented surge of retail investors entering India’s capital markets, fueled by discount brokerages and mobile investment applications, has democratized a financial terrain once dominated by institutional elites. This digital wave has funneled domestic savings away from traditional low-yield assets like gold and fixed deposits directly into equity markets, providing vital capital to Indian enterprises. However, this rapid financialization introduces severe systemic risks, primarily driven by the behavioral vulnerabilities of inexperienced investors. Many new entrants treat equity markets as speculative spaces, engaging in high-risk options trading and leveraged intraday bets driven by unverified social media influencers. This trend is worsened by a complete lack of financial literacy regarding market cycles, valuation metrics, and risk management practices. A sharp market correction could lead to severe capital losses for millions of middle-class households, damaging long-term faith in the financial system. Securing this retail investment wave requires strong regulations on financial influencers, mandatory risk disclosure tools on trading apps, and deep systemic efforts to turn speculative traders into long-term, informed investors.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: When we begin to study a phenomenon, we do not actually know what we are studying. In order to learn more about it, we formulate a hypothesis. It is important to keep in mind, however, that until we thoroughly test our hypothesis and compare the results of our experiments with its predictions, we are not on solid ground. Of course, where there are gaps in our knowledge, we must have a hypothesis, but we must also test that hypothesis—rigorously and with an uncompromising regard for the truth. Where the hypothesis is inaccurate, we must do more research. The hypothesis of the industrial civilization was that by acquiring and consuming more things we would become more happy, fulfilled, and healthy. Every day, this seems less likely.

questions.q: The entry of retail investors into India's capital markets was mainly accelerated by:
opts: Discount brokerages and mobile investment apps.
Institutions giving up control of equity.
Laws banning individual ownership of gold.
questions.why: Detail: the first sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: A positive economic outcome of this surge, according to the text, is:
opts: Domestic savings flowing into equity and providing capital to enterprises.
questions.why: Detail: the second sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author is concerned that many inexperienced investors view the stock market as:
opts: A conservative arena for preserving wealth.
A speculative playground driven by social-media advice.
questions.why: Detail: the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The word "democratized" in the first sentence means that the market has been:
opts: made open and accessible to ordinary people
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: once 'dominated by institutional elites', it is now open to retail investors. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the final sentence, protecting new retail investors requires:
opts: Regulating financial influencers and adding risk-disclosure tools to apps.
questions.why: Detail: the last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which word in the passage means "an untested idea suggested as an explanation for something"?
questions.why: Vocabulary from the passage. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: According to the passage, we must formulate a hypothesis when we
questions.why: Detail: 'where there are gaps in our knowledge, we must have a hypothesis'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "absolute, unyielding"?
questions.why: Vocabulary: 'an uncompromising regard for the truth'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: In "compare the results of our experiments with its predictions", "its" refers to
questions.why: Reference question: 'its' points back to 'our hypothesis'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: What does the author suggest about the hypothesis of industrial civilization?
opts: It is increasingly unlikely to be true
questions.why: Inference: 'Every day, this seems less likely.' Note the hedged answer, not 'certainly false'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: She is more intelligent of the two sisters.
She is the more intelligent of the two sisters.
She is the most intelligenter of the two sisters.
She is the most intelligent of the two sisters.
questions.why: With two, use the comparative with 'the': 'the more … of the two'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the incorrect sentence:
opts: The cattle are grazing in the field.
The jury has given its verdict.
questions.why: 'News' is uncountable and singular: 'The news is encouraging'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: The doctor said to me, “Take this medicine twice a day.”
opts: The doctor said me to take this medicine twice a day.
The doctor told that I take that medicine twice a day.
The doctor advised me to take that medicine twice a day.
The doctor advised me that take the medicine twice a day.
questions.why: Advice or orders become told/advised + object + to-infinitive; this → that. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “You ______ have told me earlier; I could have helped.”
questions.why: 'Should have' + past participle expresses a past action that was advisable but not done. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “ameliorate”:
questions.why: Ameliorate = make better. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram, inaugurated on 1 August 2026, is in which state?
questions.why: Vizianagaram district, Andhra Pradesh. Commercial operations began on 17 August 2026.

questions.q: 'Samudra Manthan', a ₹84,084-crore scheme approved in 2026, is for:
questions.why: Runs till 2030-31. Aug 2026.

questions.q: Smriti Mandhana scored 124 off 64 balls in the 2026 Women's T20 Asia Cup against:
Who won India's first medal at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.why: India finished fourth with 39 medals.

questions.q: The International Day of Peace is observed on:
questions.why: 10 December is Human Rights Day.

questions.q: Dudhsagar waterfalls are on which river?
questions.why: On the Goa–Karnataka border.

questions.q: Who became Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff on 1 August 2026?
The National SC-ST Hub, which supports SC and ST entrepreneurs, is run by the Ministry of:
Who won the Nobel Peace Prize 2026?
questions.why: The South African jurist and former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of these states?
questions.why: It crosses Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 100, 96, 88, 76, 60, ?
questions.why: The amounts subtracted are 4, 8, 12, 16, then 20: 60 - 20 = 40.

questions.q: Which letter is eighth to the right of the fifteenth letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.why: The fifteenth letter is O. Eight places on is the twenty-third letter, W.

questions.q: In a certain code PEN is written as QGQ. How is INK written in that code?
questions.why: The letters move forward by 1, 2 and 3 places: I-J, N-P, K-N.

questions.q: 6 is to 42 as 8 is to:
questions.why: 42 is 6 x 7. In the same way 8 x 9 = 72.

questions.q: Introducing a man, a woman said, 'His wife is the only daughter of my father.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.why: The only daughter of her father is the woman herself, so the man is her husband.

questions.q: The Collectorate is due north of the bus stand. The court is due east of the Collectorate. In which direction is the bus stand from the court?
questions.why: From the court, the bus stand lies to the west and to the south, that is, south-west.

questions.q: The sum of the ages of a father and his son is 60 years. The father is 40 years older than the son. What are their ages?
questions.why: Son = (60 − 40) ÷ 2 = 10; father 50. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: If A = 1, B = 2, …, Z = 26, what is the sum of the letters in COMPUTER?
At what time between 3 and 4 o’clock will the hands of a clock be at right angles (after 3:00)?
questions.why: 5.5M − 90 = 90, so M = 32 8/11: about 3:32. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Who compiled 'The Guiding Symptoms of our Materia Medica'?
questions.why: Constantine Hering's Guiding Symptoms runs to ten volumes. Kent wrote the Lectures on Homoeopathic Materia Medica, Boericke the Pocket Manual and Allen the Keynotes.

questions.q: The main source of the symptoms recorded in homoeopathic Materia Medica is:
opts: provings of drugs on healthy human beings
questions.why: Materia Medica is built chiefly from provings on healthy people, supplemented by toxicology and clinical observation.

questions.q: Which remedy is described as the chronic of Ignatia?
questions.why: Natrum mur. is the chronic of Ignatia; both cover ailments from grief, with Natrum mur. for the deep, long-standing state.

questions.q: Which remedy is inimical to Phosphorus and should not be given immediately before or after it?
questions.why: Causticum and Phosphorus are inimical. Arsenicum album is complementary to Phosphorus.

questions.q: Which remedy is regarded as the chronic of Pulsatilla?
questions.why: Silicea is the chronic of Pulsatilla. The two share a yielding, mild temperament and similar discharges.

questions.q: Aggravation from the slightest motion, with relief from pressure and from lying on the painful side, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Bryonia is worse from any motion and better from pressure. Rhus tox has the opposite modality, better from continued motion.

questions.q: A feeling that the heart will stop beating unless the patient keeps moving is a keynote of:
questions.why: Gelsemium fears the heart will stop unless he moves. Digitalis has the reverse: the heart will stop if he moves.

questions.q: Complaints of sudden, violent onset after exposure to dry, cold wind, with intense fear of death and restlessness, call for:
questions.why: Aconite: sudden onset after dry cold wind, fear of death, anxiety and restlessness. Belladonna is sudden too, but marked by heat, redness and throbbing.

questions.q: Intolerance of milk in infants, with the milk vomited in large curds soon after feeding, indicates:
questions.why: Aethusa's keynote is inability to digest milk, vomited in curds, followed by exhaustion and sleep.

questions.q: After an injury the patient says nothing is the matter with him, the bed feels too hard, and the whole body feels sore and bruised. The remedy is:
questions.why: Arnica: sore, bruised feeling, the bed feels too hard, and the patient insists he is well.

questions.q: In a typhoid state the patient feels his body is scattered about the bed and tries to gather the pieces together. The remedy is:
questions.why: This delusion is the classic keynote of Baptisia, alongside dusky face, offensive discharges and stupor.

questions.q: One cheek red and hot, the other pale and cold; the child is extremely irritable during dentition and wants to be carried. The remedy is:
questions.why: Chamomilla: one cheek red, the other pale, intolerable irritability and pain, quieted only by being carried.

questions.q: Constant nausea that is not relieved by vomiting, with a clean tongue, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Ipecac: persistent nausea, vomiting gives no relief, and the tongue stays clean. Antimonium crudum has a thick white tongue.

questions.q: For punctured wounds where the injured part is cold to the touch yet relieved by cold applications, the indicated remedy is:
questions.why: The remedy is Ledum palustre, which is not among options A to D. Coldness of the part with relief from cold is its keynote.

questions.q: Agonising colic that is relieved by bending double and by hard pressure, often brought on by anger, calls for:
questions.why: Colocynth: colic better bending double and from hard pressure, often after anger. Dioscorea is better from bending backwards.

questions.q: Profuse, painless, gushing diarrhoea that is worse in the early morning suggests:
questions.why: Podophyllum: profuse, painless, gushing, offensive stools, worse early morning. Veratrum album has diarrhoea with collapse and cold sweat.

questions.q: Stiffness and pain that are worse on first motion, better from continued motion and worse in cold, damp weather point to:
questions.why: Rhus tox: the rusty-gate modality, worse on beginning to move, better by continued motion, worse from damp cold.

questions.q: A left-sided neuralgic headache that rises and falls with the sun is characteristic of:
questions.why: Spigelia covers left-sided neuralgia increasing and decreasing with the sun. Sanguinaria has the right-sided version.

questions.q: Ailments from suppressed anger and indignation, along with clean incised wounds, call for:
questions.why: Staphisagria: effects of suppressed anger, humiliation or indignation, and incised wounds, including surgical ones.

questions.q: Burning pains relieved by heat, great anxiety and restlessness, aggravation after midnight, and thirst for small quantities at short intervals indicate:
questions.why: These are the classic generals of Arsenicum album, together with prostration out of proportion to the illness.

questions.q: Desire for cold drinks, which are vomited as soon as they become warm in the stomach, is a keynote of:
questions.why: Phosphorus craves cold drinks and vomits them once they warm in the stomach.

questions.q: Coarse rattling of mucus in the chest with very little expectoration is characteristic of:
questions.why: Antimonium tart.: loud rattling, little expectoration, drowsiness and weakness, especially in children and the old.

questions.q: Anticipatory anxiety with hurriedness, and a craving for sweets which disagree and cause diarrhoea, indicate:
questions.why: Argentum nitricum: hurried, anxious before events, craves sweets, which bring on flatulence and diarrhoea.

questions.q: Extreme chilliness, so that the patient wants the head covered even in summer, with offensive discharges and despair of recovery, calls for:
questions.why: Psorinum is very chilly, wants warm clothing in summer, has filthy-smelling discharges and despairs of recovery. Sulphur is a hot patient.

questions.q: In septic states, a pulse out of proportion to the temperature is the keynote of:
questions.why: Pyrogenium, prepared from decomposed meat, covers septic fevers with a pulse that does not match the temperature.
